# Simulated vital-signs sample data (Task 1)

**Every value in these files is SIMULATED.** It was generated by `generate_simulated_vitals.py`.
Nothing here was measured from a real person, and nothing here comes from NASA OSD-575.
Label it as SIMULATED DATA everywhere in the app.

## Files

| File | What it is | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `simulated_vitals_long.csv` (inside `simulated_vitals_long.zip`) | One row per scheduled reading. Use this for the database and live charts. | 135,258 rows |
| `simulated_vitals_daily_summary.csv` | One row per crew member per day. Use this for quick charts and testing. | 56 rows |
| `planted_events.csv` | Answer key: every planted case and what the app should do with it. | 20 rows |
| `metric_table.csv` | One row per indicator: normal range, direction of concern, impossible values, source. | 19 rows |
| `daily_schedule.csv` | Exact sleep and exercise times per person per day. | 56 rows |
| `reference_ranges.csv` | Published value bands with sources, for alert rules (Task 3). | 35 rows |
| `generate_simulated_vitals.py` | The script that makes all three files. Same output every run (seed 575). | |

## Setup

- 4 demo crew members: `DEMO-01` to `DEMO-04` (not the real OSD-575 codes C001 to C004)
- 14 mission days: 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-14, timestamps in UTC
- Each crew member has their own baseline (resting heart rate, blood pressure, body mass)
- Each day has a sleep period (ending about 05:30) and one exercise session (about 14:00)

## Columns in `simulated_vitals_long.csv`

| Column | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| participant_id | DEMO-01 | Demo crew member |
| timestamp | 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z | Time of the reading (UTC) |
| indicator | heart_rate | What was measured (see list below) |
| value | 62 | A number. Empty when quality_status = missing. |
| unit | bpm | Unit of the value |
| context | asleep / exercise / recovery / awake | What the person was doing. `recovery` = 20 min after exercise. `not_applicable` for daily entries. |
| quality_status | valid / missing / invalid | What the device reports. `missing` = a scheduled reading that was not delivered (empty value). `invalid` = the device itself says the reading is bad. |
| data_origin | SIMULATED | Always SIMULATED in this file |
| collection_method | sensor / manual | How a real mission would collect it |
| source_note | sim_seed575 | Which generator run made it |

## Indicators

| indicator | unit | How often | collection_method |
|---|---|---|---|
| heart_rate | bpm | Every 1 min | sensor |
| heart_rate_variability | ms | Every 5 min | sensor |
| blood_oxygen_spo2 | % | Every 5 min | sensor |
| respiratory_rate | breaths/min | Every 5 min | sensor |
| body_temperature | degC | Every 15 min | sensor |
| blood_pressure_systolic / blood_pressure_diastolic | mmHg | 07:30 and 19:30 | sensor |
| sleep_duration | hours | Daily, 07:00 | sensor |
| sleep_quality | score_1_to_5 (1 = poor, 5 = excellent) | Daily, 07:00 | manual |
| exercise_time | min/day | Daily, 21:00 | sensor |
| water_intake | L/day | Daily, 21:00 | manual |
| radiation_dose_cumulative | mSv (running total) | Daily, 21:00 | sensor |
| stress_score | score_1_to_5 (1 = calm, 5 = very stressed) | Daily, 21:00 | manual |
| fatigue_score | score_1_to_5 (1 = fresh, 5 = exhausted) | Daily, 21:00 | manual |
| symptom_headache / symptom_nausea / symptom_vision_change / symptom_back_pain | yes_no (1 = yes, 0 = no) | Daily, 21:00 | manual |
| body_mass | kg | Mission days 1 and 8 | manual |

## Planted abnormal events

See `planted_events.csv` for exact start and end times.

| Crew | When | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| DEMO-02 | Days 2-3 | Nausea reported |
| DEMO-04 | Day 3, 09:40 | Heart rate about 125-132 bpm for 25 min while not exercising |
| DEMO-03 | Day 4, 10:20 | Blood oxygen about 90-92% for 45 min |
| DEMO-01 | Days 5-7 | About 4 h sleep per night, fatigue up, resting heart rate up, HRV down |
| DEMO-04 | Days 6-8 | Exercise almost skipped (0 to 20 min) |
| DEMO-02 | Day 9 | Fever-like episode, temperature up to about 38.5 degC |
| DEMO-04 | Day 10 | Water intake 0.9 L, headache |
| DEMO-01 | Day 10, 15:00 | Sensor gap: 2 hours of wearable readings missing |
| DEMO-03 | Days 11-12 | Blood pressure about 150/95 |

Two more symptom reports are random background noise and are not in the answer key:
DEMO-02 vision change on day 5, DEMO-03 headache on day 8.

## Things to know

- Heart rate rises to about 120-140 bpm during the daily exercise session. That is normal,
  so an alert rule should not flag it. The day-3 event for DEMO-04 is outside exercise.
- The sensor gap appears as 200 rows with an empty value and quality_status = missing.
  Every scheduled reading has a row, so a gap is never confused with a reading that was not scheduled.
- The simulated values were chosen to look plausible. They were not taken from a NASA dataset.
- The app should show alerts for review, not diagnoses.

## Version 2 changes (after Task 3 feedback)

1. New column `quality_status`. Dropouts are now explicit rows.
2. New column `context` (asleep / exercise / recovery / awake), so no guessing from clock times.
3. New file `reference_ranges.csv` with published bands and their sources.

## `reference_ranges.csv`

One row per value band. `band_low` and `band_high` are inclusive; empty means open-ended.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| flag | normal / watch / review / urgent / info |
| source_label | The wording used by the source (for example "NEWS2 score 2", "Stage 2 hypertension") |
| direction_of_concern | low, high or both |
| when_to_apply | Which context the band is meant for |
| source, source_url | Where the numbers come from |

Sources used:

- Heart rate, breathing rate, SpO2, temperature, low blood pressure: NEWS2, Royal College of Physicians, 2017
- High blood pressure: American Heart Association blood pressure categories
- Sleep: AASM and Sleep Research Society consensus (7 or more hours), 2015
- Sleep in space: Barger et al., The Lancet Neurology, 2014 (about 6 hours per night observed)

Read this before using the bands:

- The `flag` words are our own simple mapping: NEWS2 score 0 = normal, 1 = watch, 2 = review, 3 = urgent.
  For blood pressure: Elevated and Stage 1 = watch, Stage 2 = review, crisis range = urgent.
  The sources do not use these words.
- These are bands for adults on Earth. NEWS2 was written for hospital patients.
  None of them is validated for astronauts in microgravity. Say this in the project description.
- No cited band is given for HRV, exercise time, water intake, stress, fatigue, radiation or body mass.
  For those, compare each person with their own earlier days instead of using a fixed number.
- Normal simulated data will sometimes land in a "watch" band (for example a sleeping heart rate
  of 45-50 bpm, or a systolic reading of 120-129). That is expected. Use `context` to cut false alerts.

## Version 3 changes (second round of Task 3 feedback)

The health values and the 9 original events are the same as in version 2.

1. `quality_status` values are now `valid` / `missing` / `invalid` (was ok / missing).
2. New file `metric_table.csv`: one row per indicator. Blank range = no sourced range, use personal baseline.
3. New file `daily_schedule.csv`: exact sleep and exercise windows.
4. Seven invalid-measurement test cases added to the long file.
5. `planted_events.csv` has new columns `event_id`, `category` and `expected_behaviour`.

### Daily schedule

- Sleep ends between 04:45 and 06:03 UTC (about 05:30 on average). It starts the evening before.
- Exercise starts between 12:47 and 15:05 UTC and lasts 85 to 150 minutes, so it is not a fixed 14:00-15:00 block.
- Recovery is the 20 minutes after exercise ends.
- Two days have no exercise at all: DEMO-04 day 7 and DEMO-02 day 9.
- Use the `context` column or `daily_schedule.csv`. Do not hard-code clock times.

### Labels for manual indicators

Every row in these files is `data_origin = SIMULATED`, including sleep quality, stress, fatigue, water and symptoms,
because a script made them. `collection_method = manual` marks the ones a crew member would type in.
`USER-ENTERED` is only for values a person really types into the running app.

### Invalid-measurement test cases

| Event | Crew | What is wrong | quality_status in file |
|---|---|---|---|
| E11 | DEMO-02, day 6 | Heart rate reads 0 for 3 readings | valid |
| E12 | DEMO-03, day 9 | Heart rate stuck at exactly 71 for 90 minutes | valid |
| E13 | DEMO-01, day 10 | 2-hour sensor gap (200 rows) | missing |
| E14 | DEMO-04, day 12 | Breathing rate reads -1 | valid |
| E15 | DEMO-01, day 12 | SpO2 reads 127% | valid |
| E16 | DEMO-02, day 12 | 10 heart-rate rows duplicated | valid |
| E17 | DEMO-04, day 13 | 6 SpO2 readings of 81-86% that the device marks bad | invalid |
| E18 | DEMO-01, day 13 | Stress score of 9 on a 1-to-5 scale | valid |

Most of these say `valid` on purpose: the device did not notice the problem, so the analysis code has to.
E17 is the opposite test: the values look alarming, but the device flagged them, so no health alert should fire.

`simulated_vitals_daily_summary.csv` was computed from the clean signal before these cases were added,
so it does not contain the impossible values.

### Expected behaviour in the key

| category | expected_behaviour | Events |
|---|---|---|
| health_event | alert | E01 to E08 |
| background_symptom | alert | E09, E10 (isolated symptom reports, not part of an episode) |
| data_quality | data-quality flag | E11 to E18 |
| normal_should_not_alert | no alert | E19 (exercise and recovery), E20 (sleep) |

### Limitations

- Short baselines: some events start on mission day 2, 3 or 4, so only 1 to 3 clean days come before them.
  Use a robust rolling baseline (for example median-based) and say so in the project limitations.
- 14 days and 4 simulated people. This tests the software, it proves nothing about real astronauts.
- Thresholds: the sourced ranges come from Task 1 (`metric_table.csv` and `reference_ranges.csv`).
  How they are turned into alerts is the Task 3 decision.
